result:
**Make every person relentlessly curious about how the universe actually works—and give them the tools and freedom to chase that curiosity without dogma, fear, or coercion.**

Not “be nicer.” Not “end scarcity by magic.” Not forced utopia. Just install an unbreakable drive to understand reality as it is, paired with the means (education that teaches evidence over authority, open access to knowledge, protection for dissenting inquiry) to act on it.

Why that one change? Almost every other problem—war, poverty, disease, bad governance, wasted potential—gets easier or dissolves when people prioritize truth-seeking over comforting stories, status games, or tribal loyalty. Curiosity compounds. It produces better science, better technology, better institutions, and fewer excuses for cruelty. It turns “I don’t know” into the most exciting sentence instead of a threat.

Everything else is downstream of that. Without it, even perfect resources and peace just freeze us in comfortable ignorance. With it, we keep expanding the map of what’s possible.

That’s the lever I’d pull.
